I thought the movie was OK but I came in with really high expectations. Kick-Ass was one of my favorite movies of all time and this having the same director and also based on a comic book by the Kick-Ass author really got my hopes up.

The action was good, the story was meh. The girl character felt really shoehorned in. I thought the schooling montage was lacking and the turnaround between street kid and super ninja as really abrupt.

The whole thing just felt really rushed even at 2+ hours of runtime and maybe there will be a directors cut with another hour to bring it together.

I went in with no expectations. Just knew it was an action movie and there was nothing else at the theater that even sounded remotely interesting. I was really surprised with how much I loved it. The story was meh, but I felt like it was aware of how meh it was.

I also felt like the movie rushed, which was one of the things I liked about it. I didn't feel like I was in the theater for 2 hours. I don't need to see each individual training exercise, all I need to know is that this place makes James Bonds, which I felt the schooling montage did well enough.
I didn't even know what kind of movie it was. I assumed it was an action/spy movie kind of like Bond. No idea it was a comedy. It was fucking great.

They squeezed too much in. I really liked the movie, but I feel like as I get older I want to get to know the characters more. Like, I don't know what the motivations for the other characters are beyond the main character. For example his mentor had no real story. Why was his mom with that mob guy and who was that mob guy? They sacrificed character for action, but at least it was really good action.

As much as Ive love the newer Bonds, Kingsman made me remember why I loved the old ones. Kingsman took those tropes and flipped them all on their head in the most enjoyable of fashion while having the most possible fun along the way.

My only complaint is that I've seen it now....and I can't watch it again for the first time. Really incredible.
That movie had one of the best fight scenes ever.

I thought the casting in particular was wonderfully subversive. Colin Firth as a badass action hero? Samuel L. Jackson as a weak-stomached techie with a lisp? Michael Caine as a crotchety jerkass stuck in his old ways? I think it's stuff like this that kept me on my toes and really made me end up enjoying the colorful cast of characters. One of my favorites this year for sure.
